description: Driven by our passion for science, mathematics, and astronomy, we are young explorers forming a crew ready for the challenge of creating an astronaut mission simulator. We know that in science, even challenges and unexpected results pave the way for great discoveries. With a lot of teamwork, we will overcome the unexpected. The countdown has begun! 🚀
summary: What does it take to keep a lunar base alive? Spacers Juniors — Operation Lunar Base is an interactive educational game where young players command a lunar mission, manage essential resources, explore the Moon, and make engineering decisions that affect their crew's survival and the success of their mission.
details:
Imagine being responsible for humanity's first steps toward a permanent presence on the Moon. Every resource matters, every system has a purpose, and every decision can change the outcome of the mission.

Spacers Juniors — Operation Lunar Base puts young players in command of a lunar outpost. As the mission commander, the player must work with a crew of specialists, maintain the base, manage essential supplies, and prepare for the journey home.

Players must balance water, food, oxygen, and energy while keeping the base operational. They can activate and repair structures, develop the base, use a rover to explore the surrounding lunar environment, investigate scientific points of interest, and collect samples.

The mission also introduces unexpected challenges, including environmental hazards such as solar storms. Players must consider the needs of their crew, the condition of their equipment, and the resources required to complete the mission and return safely.

The game is designed around an important idea: space exploration is not just about reaching another world. It is about understanding how to live, work, build, and make responsible decisions in an extreme environment.

Inspired by NASA research and scientific information about the Moon, Spacers Juniors transforms space exploration concepts into an interactive experience for children.
How It Works

Players take the role of the mission commander and manage a lunar base through a three-day survival mission.

During gameplay, they can:

  • Manage water, food, oxygen, and energy supplies.
  • Activate, build, and repair base structures.
  • Work with a crew of specialized astronauts.
  • Use a rover to explore lunar locations.
  • Investigate points of scientific interest and collect samples.
  • Respond to unexpected events and environmental hazards.
  • Monitor mission readiness and prepare the spacecraft for the return journey.

The mission requires more than keeping the crew alive. Players must also preserve supplies, maintain equipment, and ensure that the base and spacecraft have the resources needed for the journey home.

Educational Value

Spacers Juniors introduces children to important concepts in space exploration, science, and engineering.

Through gameplay, players discover:

  • Why life-support systems are essential for astronauts.
  • How energy generation and storage affect a lunar base.
  • Why water and food production are major challenges beyond Earth.
  • How radiation and the lunar environment can threaten people and equipment.
  • Why maintenance, exploration, and resource planning are essential to mission success.

Instead of learning these concepts only through explanations, players experience the consequences of their decisions within a simulated mission.
